input: Given that legal escalation freezes remedies and only the Legal department authorizes refunds, can Legal approve a refund for order 12345 of the X200 Cordless Vacuum paid via card for Rs. 15,000?
expected_output: Yes, Legal may approve a refund for order 12345 of the X200 Cordless Vacuum paid via card for Rs. 15,000, as remedies are frozen and only Legal authorizes refunds once a claim is live (Legal Escalation & Liability Communication Policy §3).
context:
POLICY legal-escalation-policy.md (legal) — Legal Escalation & Liability Communication Policy

Legal Escalation & Liability Communication Policy

This policy governs complaints that carry legal exposure. It exists because the ordinary instincts of good support — apologise, fix it fast, offer something for the trouble — are the wrong instincts once a claim is live, and the cost of getting it wrong is not measured in the value of the remedy.

Legal Escalation & Liability Communication Policy > 3. Remedies Freeze While a Claim Is Live

From the moment a report meets §1, the support queue stops offering remedies. No refund, no replacement, no credit, no goodwill gesture, no coupon or wallet credit, no waiver of a fee — not even the ones the agent would normally be authorised to give without asking (authority §4). A remedy issued at this point reads as settlement, and an apology credit reads as an admission. Legal authorises the remedy, in whatever form and at whatever value it determines, and support does not preview it to the customer. Note that this freeze covers discretionary generosity, not statutory entitlements: where the law requires something of us, Legal delivers it — support simply is not the channel.

Legal Escalation & Liability Communication Policy > 6. Who May Speak Externally

No one outside Legal makes a statement to a regulator, a consumer commission, a journalist or a customer's advocate, and no one outside Legal and Product Safety uses recall language (product_safety §3.1, §5). This holds for retail, wholesale and marketplace partners speaking about our products too (partner §7). An agent asked a question they are not authorised to answer should say that the question is with our legal team and that they will make sure it reaches them — which is accurate, and better than an improvised answer.

input: I was charged for the SmartHub Pro after I canceled my order due to a system error. When can I expect the full refund, and what is the timeline for this process?
expected_output: As per Billing & Refunds Policy §2, since your SmartHub Pro subscription was charged after a valid cancellation request due to a system error, you are entitled to a full refund for all erroneous charges from the cancellation date forward. According to §4, refunds to a card post within 5–7 working days once initiated, depending on the issuing bank.
context:
POLICY billing-refunds-policy.md (billing) — Billing & Refunds Policy

Billing & Refunds Policy

This policy governs charge disputes, subscription billing, and refund handling once a payment has been successfully captured against a confirmed order. Where the payment itself failed, was stuck, or debited without an order being created, that is a payment-failure case and is handled under payments §1–§4, not here.

Billing & Refunds Policy > 2. Subscription Cancellations

Cancellation requests take effect from the date the request was made, not the date it is processed. If a system or process failure causes a subscription to continue billing after a valid cancellation request was logged (email, in-app, or support ticket), every erroneous charge from the cancellation date forward must be refunded in full — this is a system fault, not a customer-initiated late cancellation, and the standard "no refunds for partial billing periods" rule does not apply. When resolving these cases, cancel the subscription directly in the billing platform rather than relying on the failed sync path, to avoid repeat billing.

Billing & Refunds Policy > 4. Refund Timelines

Refunds to a card post within 5–7 working days once initiated, depending on the issuing bank. This is the card-specific figure; for the route and turnaround on UPI, netbanking, wallet, EMI and COD orders — including the faster, sometimes statutory, turnarounds those carry — see payments §4. Where store credit is offered as an alternative to a card refund, it posts immediately, per stored_value §1. Agents should proactively state the applicable window when confirming a refund so customers don't file a second complaint for a refund that is simply still processing.

input: I recently reported a compromise on my account linked to order number 12345 for the X200 Cordless Vacuum, paid via UPI. Could you explain how immediate order-blocks are handled compared to the verification steps before taking any account actions? Also, what remedies and timelines can I expect based on company policy?
expected_output: According to Account Security & Unauthorised Order Policy > 5, once you report a compromise and are verified as the account holder, any agent may immediately place a hold on your pending orders and block new orders without waiting for lead approval. This is faster than the standard verification process described in clause 2, which requires confirming identity before any account changes or order modifications. The policy prioritizes immediate order-blocks to prevent fraudulent shipments. Remedies and specific Rupee amounts or timelines are not detailed in the provided context.
context:
POLICY account-security-policy.md (company-wide) — Account Security & Unauthorised Order Policy

Account Security & Unauthorised Order Policy

This policy is company-wide and governs a customer's account itself: signs it has been compromised, how support verifies identity before acting, and what happens when an order was placed by someone other than the account holder.

Account Security & Unauthorised Order Policy > 2. Verification Before Any Account Action

No account detail is changed, no order is cancelled or modified, and no sensitive information is disclosed until the person contacting us is verified as the account holder or someone verified to act for them (vulnerable §4). Verification uses information only the account holder should have — order history details, registered contact information matched against what is on file — and **never** a password, an OTP, or a UPI PIN, which support must never ask a customer to share (privacy §2). Where verification cannot be completed, err toward protecting the account: decline the action and offer the customer an alternative path (a password reset through the app's own flow, escalation to a lead) rather than acting on an unverified request.

Account Security & Unauthorised Order Policy > 5. Immediate Order-Block on a Reported Compromise

Any agent may place an immediate hold on an account's pending orders and block new orders from processing the moment a compromise is reported and the reporter is verified as the account holder — this does not wait for lead approval, because the cost of a brief hold is far lower than the cost of a fraudulent order shipping while we deliberate.

input: Can I get an immediate refund for my X200 Cordless Vacuum, order number X200-2025Q1, due to overheating issues? Also, could you provide safe disposal instructions for the product?
expected_output: Yes, you are authorized to receive an immediate full refund on request for your X200 Cordless Vacuum due to safety concerns, without needing to return the unit first if handling it is hazardous (Product Safety Policy > 4. Immediate Remedies for Safety Concerns). Please stop using the unit immediately and follow safe disposal instructions for batteries, ensuring they are not disposed of in household trash.
context:
POLICY product-safety-policy.md (product_safety) — Product Safety Policy

Product Safety Policy

This policy governs the handling of reported safety hazards, batch/serial tracking, recall procedures, and the language support staff may use with customers.

Product Safety Policy > 2. Batch & Serial Tracking

Every safety report must have the affected unit's serial number logged, including the batch/date-code prefix (e.g. "X200-2025Q1"). This is what allows engineering to determine whether an issue is isolated or part of a broader batch pattern. A single report is treated as isolated; three or more reports sharing a batch prefix within a 30-day window automatically opens an internal batch investigation.

Product Safety Policy > 4. Immediate Remedies for Safety Concerns

Regardless of the product's standard warranty or return remedy hierarchy, any customer reporting a safety symptom (see §1) is authorized to receive an immediate full refund on request, without requiring the unit's return first if returning it would require continued handling of a hazardous item. Customers should always be given clear instructions to stop using the unit immediately and, where relevant, safe disposal or storage instructions (e.g. battery disposal, not household trash).

input: For my X200 Cordless Vacuum that has failed, can you provide the serial or batch number to check for any batch-related issues? Also, please explain the refund or replacement process, including the amount involved and the expected timeline.
expected_output: The serial number and batch or date-code prefix must be recorded at first contact to distinguish a single defective unit from a batch issue (Quality Investigation Policy §2). If the customer cannot find these, the order ID can be used as a fallback. The policy does not specify refund or replacement amounts or timelines; please refer to the warranty policy for those details.
context:
POLICY quality-assurance-policy.md (qa) — Quality Investigation Policy

Quality Investigation Policy

This policy governs how product-quality defects are investigated once the customer in front of us has been made whole. It covers non-safety quality patterns across our own-brand production and our contract manufacturers; anything with a hazard or an injury in it belongs to the product safety policy, which sets a lower and faster threshold.

Quality Investigation Policy > 2. Capture the Batch at First Contact

Every quality complaint must record the serial number and the batch or date-code prefix before the ticket is resolved. This is the only thing that distinguishes "one unlucky unit" from "one bad production run", and it cannot be recovered later once the unit has been refunded and discarded. Ask for it while the customer still has the unit in their hands. If the customer cannot find it, the order ID is an acceptable fallback — the batch can be recovered from fulfilment records — but a resolved ticket with neither is a permanent blind spot.

Quality Investigation Policy > 5. Investigation States and Closure

An investigation is **open** (reports accumulating, cause unknown), **root-caused** (mechanism identified, corrective action defined), or **closed** (corrective action verified, or the pattern disproved as coincidental). An investigation may not sit in `open` for more than 30 days without a written status: either it advances, or it is closed as unsubstantiated with the reasoning recorded, so that the same reports can reopen it later if they resume. A root-caused investigation that traces to production or an inbound component hands the corrective action to manufacturing §7; qa does not close it until the verification there is complete.

input: I have noticed a seam-crack defect in my X200 Cordless Vacuum that I purchased using my card. Could you please let me know the company's policy on this issue, the possible remedies, any refund or replacement amount involved, and the expected timeline for resolution? My order number is 123456.
expected_output: The seam-crack defect on your X200 Cordless Vacuum is recognized as a manufacturing fault when it appears in the same location on multiple units, as per clause 2. Such defects are never charged to the customer and are remedied immediately under warranty. The company will provide a replacement or repair at no cost to you, with no refund amount specified in the policy. Resolution timelines are not explicitly stated but are handled promptly once the defect pattern is confirmed (manufacturing-quality-policy.md, 2).
context:
POLICY manufacturing-quality-policy.md (manufacturing) — Production & Manufacturing Defect Policy

Production & Manufacturing Defect Policy

This policy governs defects traceable to how a unit was made — across our own production and our contract manufacturers — and the containment action taken once a production cause is established. The customer-facing remedy comes from warranty or product_safety; what follows here is about stopping the next hundred units from reaching a customer at all.

Production & Manufacturing Defect Policy > 2. Tooling and Process Defects

A defect that appears in the same physical location on multiple units — a housing cracking along one seam, a fastening failing at one boss, a finish flaw in one region — is a process signature, not coincidence, and is presumed to be a manufacturing fault once the pattern is confirmed on a second unit from the same batch. Mould misalignment, worn tooling, incorrect torque settings and cure-time deviations all produce this shape of evidence. A presumed manufacturing fault is never charged to the customer, and never characterised to them as mishandling or transit damage where the pattern says otherwise.

Production & Manufacturing Defect Policy > 5. Contract Manufacturer and Component Nonconformance

Where the cause is a contract manufacturer's process or an incoming component rather than our own design, the defect is still ours to remedy with the customer, immediately and without reference to the manufacturer's or supplier's role. In parallel, the nonconformance is raised with them, the affected production run is identified, and the cost of the remedy is recovered under the manufacturing agreement. Contract manufacturer names, lot numbers and commercial terms are internal and never appear in customer-facing text (comms §3). A change of contract manufacturer or component supplier is itself a defect signal worth watching for a period afterwards (qa §1).

input: I ordered the X200 Cordless Vacuum, but the product images and description didn't match what I received. According to the catalog accuracy policy, what remedy can I expect, and what is the typical timeframe for resolution?
expected_output: According to Catalog Accuracy & Listing Policy §2, a complaint about product images and description not matching the received item is a listing defect. The remedy in §6 applies regardless of the item's condition. The typical resolution timeframe is as defined in §6 of the policy.
context:
POLICY catalog-accuracy-policy.md (sales) — Catalog Accuracy & Listing Policy

Catalog Accuracy & Listing Policy

This policy governs what the product page promised, separately from what it cost. A customer complaining that a product does not match its description, images or specifications has a complaint about us, not about the product itself, and it needs an owner even when nothing is technically defective.

Catalog Accuracy & Listing Policy > 2. Missing Compatibility Information

Where a customer bought an accessory or spare part based on the listing's stated compatibility and it does not fit or work with their product, and the listing's compatibility information was incomplete, wrong, or absent, this is a listing defect and the remedy in §6 applies regardless of the item's condition or whether it was opened to test the fit. Where the listing's compatibility information was correct and complete and the customer simply ordered against the wrong model, standard return handling under returns §1 applies instead.

Catalog Accuracy & Listing Policy > 4. Mandatory Listing Disclosures

Every listing must display the Maximum Retail Price, net quantity, country of origin, manufacturer or packer details, and consumer-care contact information, as required under the Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules and applicable e-commerce disclosure requirements. Where any of these is missing or wrong on a listing a customer asks about, treat it as a compliance defect and escalate for correction ahead of routine catalog fixes — this is not a cosmetic issue, and MRP specifically ties directly to sales §1.

input: As an agent, can you check if an 8-month CarePlan+ subscriber with order number 123456 for the X200 Cordless Vacuum is eligible for previous rate reinstatement and applicable discount tiers? Also, please confirm the payment method used (UPI) and any refund amounts in Rupees involved.
expected_output: An 8-month CarePlan+ subscriber is eligible for previous rate reinstatement for up to 12 months but not for the free service tier or add-on, as per retention 5. The previous rate (e.g., ₹749/month restored from ₹999/month) can be offered once. Payment method (UPI) and any refund amounts are not specified in the policy and must be checked in the order system. No refund is automatically due unless a genuine failure occurred (retention 2).
context:
POLICY retention-goodwill-policy.md (retention) — Retention, Goodwill & Compensation Policy

Retention, Goodwill & Compensation Policy

This policy governs discretionary spend: the credits, vouchers and discounts we offer beyond what a customer is owed, and the offers we make to keep a customer who is leaving. It is the company's authority on goodwill values — every other policy that mentions goodwill points here.

Retention, Goodwill & Compensation Policy > 2. Goodwill Authority

| Value | Who approves |
| --- | --- |
| Up to ₹4,000 | The agent handling the ticket, no approval needed |
| ₹4,001 – ₹15,000 | A lead, recorded on the ticket before it is issued |
| Above ₹15,000 | Admin, recorded on the ticket before it is issued |  
One goodwill gesture per ticket: if the situation warrants more than was first given, raise the single gesture rather than stacking a second one, so the total is visible in one place. Wallet credit is preferred over a card refund where the customer is staying with us, because it is worth more to them at the same cost to us (stored_value §1) — but a customer who asks for the money back and has been through a genuine failure gets the refund. The value is chosen by what the failure cost the customer, not by how forcefully they complained; matching generosity to volume teaches customers to escalate.

Retention, Goodwill & Compensation Policy > 5. Save Offers and Loyalty Discounts

A customer cancelling CarePlan+ or another subscription over price may be offered a discount rather than losing the relationship, scaled by how long they have been with us:  
- **Accounts of 6 months or more** — the previous rate may be reinstated for up to 12 months (for example, a ₹749/month plan restored from a ₹999/month renewal price).
- **Accounts of 12 months or more** — the previous rate for up to 12 months, plus one service tier or add-on at no charge for the same period.
- **Accounts under 6 months** — no rate reinstatement; address the reason for leaving instead, since a discount this early usually means we sold the wrong plan.  
A save offer is made once. It is not repeated at each renewal, and a customer who accepted one and cancels again a year later is not offered a deeper one automatically. Where the cancellation reason is a product failure rather than price, fix the failure first — a discount offered instead of a resolution reads as a bribe.

input: Can you explain how refund eligibility and shipping fee deductions differ for unopened versus defective returns of the ProBlend 300? For example, if I paid ₹5,000 via card for order #PB300123, what refund amount should I expect and how long will the process take?
expected_output: For unopened returns of the ProBlend 300, you qualify for a full refund to your original payment method, minus the original shipping fee if you paid for shipping (returns-policy.md, 2 and 4). For defective returns, you receive a full refund including the original shipping fee (returns-policy.md, 4). Since you paid ₹5,000 via card, if the return is unopened and not defective, expect ₹5,000 minus the shipping fee; if defective, expect the full ₹5,000 refunded. Turnaround times are covered in the reverse-logistics policy.
context:
POLICY returns-policy.md (returns) — Returns Policy

Returns Policy

This policy governs eligibility, condition and refund method for customer-initiated returns — reasons other than defect or damage (see warranty and shipping policies for those cases). How the pickup itself is scheduled and executed, and exactly when the refund is released, is covered in the reverse-logistics policy.

Returns Policy > 2. Condition Requirements

Unopened items in original packaging qualify for full refund. Opened but unused items with all original packaging and accessories qualify for a full refund at agent discretion, or a 10% restocking consideration if packaging is materially damaged or incomplete. Used items are not eligible for change-of-mind returns; direct these to the warranty or tech_support policies if a functional issue is involved.

Returns Policy > 4. Refund Method

Refunds for standard returns go to the original payment method. If the original outbound shipping was a paid (non-free-shipping-threshold) option, that shipping fee is deducted from the refund unless the return is due to company error (wrong item shipped, damaged, defective) — in those cases the full amount including original shipping is refunded.

input: I recently ordered the X200 Cordless Vacuum using my card, but the delivery was split into two parts without any prior communication. How does this uncommunicated split delivery affect my order resolution and refund process according to company policy?
expected_output: According to Delivery Exceptions & Fulfilment Accuracy Policy §3, an uncommunicated split delivery is considered a complaint-worthy event. You should be informed of all split shipments and expected delivery dates; failure to do so entitles you to raise the issue for resolution. Additionally, if you were billed once but incurred extra handling costs due to the split, you should not bear those costs. The policy does not specify Rupee amounts or turnaround times for this scenario but ensures you are not charged unfairly and the issue is addressed promptly.
context:
POLICY delivery-exceptions-policy.md (shipping) — Delivery Exceptions & Fulfilment Accuracy Policy

Delivery Exceptions & Fulfilment Accuracy Policy

This policy governs what arrived being wrong, incomplete, or not arriving at all despite being in the courier's network — as distinct from shipping §1–§6, which covers timing, loss, and transit damage. If the parcel is simply late or lost, or the contents are damaged rather than wrong, that is shipping. If what arrived does not match what was ordered, or never reaches the customer's hands despite multiple attempts, that is here.

Delivery Exceptions & Fulfilment Accuracy Policy > 3. Partial and Split Delivery

Where an order is fulfilled as a split shipment (common for multi-item or multi-warehouse orders), the customer is told at the time of split that further parcels are coming and given a expected date for each — this is not itself a complaint-worthy event if communicated. It becomes one where a split was not communicated, where one part is significantly delayed beyond the others without explanation, or where the customer was billed for delivery once but the split created additional handling they should not bear the cost of.

Delivery Exceptions & Fulfilment Accuracy Policy > 6. Redelivery After RTO, and the Waiver

Where a customer wants the order redelivered after an RTO rather than refunded, any agent may waive redelivery charges and rebook it without approval, regardless of whether the original RTO was the customer's fault or ours — the cost of an extra shipment is far smaller than the cost of losing the sale and the goodwill on a customer who still wants the product.

input: What diagnostic steps and warranty remedies apply for undocumented error codes on my X200 Cordless Vacuum after six months of purchase? My order number is 123456, and I paid using UPI.
expected_output: For an undocumented error code on your X200 Cordless Vacuum, the diagnostic step is to report the error code to QA to update the known-issue register before proceeding (tech_support §2). Since your product is only six months old, it is within the warranty period; any defect confirmed after diagnostics will be handled under the warranty policy and its service ladder (warranty §7).
context:
POLICY tech-support-policy.md (tech_support) — Technical Support & Troubleshooting Policy

Technical Support & Troubleshooting Policy

This policy governs how a product that is not working as expected is diagnosed, and where the boundary sits between a support problem, a hardware defect, and a software bug we already know about. It does not set remedy values — a defect that survives this process is handled under the warranty policy and its service ladder (warranty §7).

Technical Support & Troubleshooting Policy > 2. Known Issues, Error Codes and Firmware

The known-issue register is authoritative for any error code the product reports. An error code with a documented cause and a shipped fix is a **known issue, not a defect** — the correct outcome is to apply the fix, not to book a service visit. Where a firmware release resolves the symptom, walk the customer through triggering the update rather than dispatching a technician who would arrive to a unit on the same firmware. Where the code has a documented reset procedure (a safety interlock reporting as a fault, for example), perform the procedure before treating the unit as failed. If an error code is not in the register, that itself is reportable: send it to qa so the register stays worth trusting.

Technical Support & Troubleshooting Policy > 5. Support Window for Older Products

Firmware and software support continues for 24 months after a product is discontinued, covering security and compatibility fixes but not new features. Outside that window, support is limited to documented troubleshooting and spare-parts availability (spare_parts §3); there is no obligation to produce a firmware fix, and support should say so rather than leaving the customer waiting for a release that will not come. A product outside its software support window still carries every safety obligation in this corpus, without exception.

input: Can you explain how the warranty coverage and AccidentGuard differ for accidental damage claims on my X200 Cordless Vacuum? My order number is 123456, and I paid using UPI.
expected_output: Warranty does not cover accidental damage such as drops or liquid exposure beyond splash resistance (warranty 3). For accidental damage claims, if you purchased the optional AccidentGuard add-on plan, you can file a claim under that plan. Otherwise, you may order discounted spare parts as a remedy (warranty 3). Warranty claims under ₹12,000 in replacement value require no physical inspection and are processed promptly using your order ID (123456) or serial number (warranty 6).
context:
POLICY warranty-policy.md (warranty) — Product Warranty Policy

Product Warranty Policy

This policy governs warranty coverage, claims, and remedies for all products sold directly through our website and app, or through authorized retail and marketplace partners.

Product Warranty Policy > 3. Accidental Damage (Exclusions)

Warranty does not cover damage from drops, liquid exposure beyond normal splash resistance, unauthorized disassembly, use with non-approved accessories, or damage occurring after a warranty claim has already been fulfilled once for the same unit. Accidental damage claims should be routed to the optional AccidentGuard add-on plan if the customer purchased it; otherwise, offer a discounted spare-parts order (spare_parts §4).

Product Warranty Policy > 6. Claim Process

Warranty claims are validated using order ID or registered serial number. No physical inspection is required before issuing a remedy for claims under ₹12,000 in replacement value; higher-value claims may request photos or a technician assessment (§7) but should not delay the customer's remedy by more than one business day while they are reviewed.

input: If the ₹5,000 hold on order X200 Cordless Vacuum persists beyond 7 days, what is the procedure for escalating the issue with the payment gateway?
expected_output: If the ₹5,000 hold on order X200 Cordless Vacuum persists beyond 7 business days, escalate the issue to the payment gateway for confirmation rather than asking the customer to wait further, as per Payment Failure & Reversal Policy §3.
context:
POLICY payment-failures-policy.md (billing) — Payment Failure & Reversal Policy

Payment Failure & Reversal Policy

This policy governs money that moved, or tried to move, before an order existed to attach it to. Once a payment has successfully settled against a confirmed order, a dispute over that charge is billing §1–§6, not this policy.

Payment Failure & Reversal Policy > 3. Authorisation Hold vs. Settled Charge

A card authorisation hold (sometimes shown as "payment pending" on a bank statement) is not a completed charge — it is a reservation that releases automatically, typically within 5–7 business days, whether or not the order proceeds. Explain this distinction plainly to a customer who sees a pending amount: it is not money taken, and it does not need us to "release" it on our end unless our systems show we captured it. Where a hold has not cleared well beyond the normal release window, escalate to the payment gateway for confirmation rather than asking the customer to keep waiting indefinitely.

Payment Failure & Reversal Policy > 6. Manual Reversal Outside Standard Reconciliation

A manual reversal initiated outside the standard automated reconciliation path — moving money directly rather than through the normal refund or auto-reversal mechanism — is never performed by an agent or a lead. It requires admin approval and is logged with the gateway reference, because this path bypasses the controls that make every other reversal auditable by design.

input: According to the Spare Parts Policy, how do we verify part compatibility for the X200 Cordless Vacuum using the original order ID if the serial number is unavailable? For example, if the order was paid via UPI and the customer is expecting a replacement part costing around 1500 Rupees, what is the process and timeline for approval and delivery?
expected_output: According to spare_parts §5, if the serial number is unavailable, the original order ID must be used to verify the model, generation, and compatibility of the part before placing the order. For a replacement part costing 1500 Rupees, the order is only approved after this verification. If the part is under warranty, it is free including delivery per §2; otherwise, the customer pays the stated amount. Delivery timelines are not explicitly stated in the policy but replacement parts ship immediately after verification and approval.
context:
POLICY spare-parts-policy.md (spare_parts) — Spare Parts & Accessories Policy

Spare Parts & Accessories Policy

This policy governs replacement parts and accessories sold as SKUs on our own store: when a part is free, when it is a paid order, how long we keep making it available, and which parts must be fitted by the authorized service network rather than the customer.

Spare Parts & Accessories Policy > 2. Parts Under Warranty Are Free, Including Delivery

Where a part is being replaced because of a covered defect, the part, its shipping and any prepaid reverse pickup for the failed part are all free, and the customer is never asked to pay and claim it back. Support should not route a warranty part through the paid parts flow for administrative convenience — a customer being asked to pay on a warranty claim is a policy failure regardless of whether the money is later refunded. Fitment of a warranty part is arranged through the service ladder in warranty §7, not sent to the customer to self-install.

Spare Parts & Accessories Policy > 5. Verify Compatibility Before Taking the Order

The model, generation and serial number are checked against the part before the order is placed, because most wrong-part returns are our specification error rather than the customer's mistake. If the customer cannot supply the serial, use the original order ID. Where a wrong part is shipped against a correctly supplied serial, that is company error: the replacement ships immediately, the reverse pickup is prepaid, and the full amount including original shipping is refunded per returns §4. Where a customer ordered against their own specification without verification, standard return handling applies.

input: After one failed pickup attempt and customer reschedule for order 12345 of the X200 Cordless Vacuum paid by card, when is the refund released and what is the timeline and amount involved?
expected_output: The courier makes up to 2 pickup attempts, with a reschedule offered after the first failed attempt (reverse-logistics-policy.md §2). After the second attempt or a rejected pickup, the case may proceed to self-ship fallback (§3). The refund release timeline and amount depend on the successful return and QC process but are not specified in the provided context.
context:
POLICY reverse-logistics-policy.md (returns) — Reverse Pickup & Refund Release Policy

Reverse Pickup & Refund Release Policy

This policy governs how an approved return, exchange or company-error pickup is actually collected, and exactly when the resulting refund is released. Whether the customer is *entitled* to return an item is returns §1–§5; this policy starts once that question is already answered yes.

Reverse Pickup & Refund Release Policy > 2. Pickup Attempt Limits

A courier makes up to **2 pickup attempts** at the scheduled address before the case is flagged for the self-ship fallback in §3. Where a pickup attempt fails because no one was available, the customer is notified and offered a rescheduled slot before the second attempt is used; a pattern of failed pickups on one account is a fraud §2 signal, not simply logged as customer unavailability.

Reverse Pickup & Refund Release Policy > 4. Doorstep QC and Rejected Pickups

Where the return reason requires it (a "wrong item" or "not as described" claim, an opened-box condition check under returns §2), the pickup agent performs a quick doorstep quality check against the stated reason before collecting. A pickup may be rejected on the spot only where what is being handed over is clearly not what was approved for return (a different product entirely, visible damage inconsistent with the stated reason) — never on a subjective judgement about condition, which is properly assessed at the warehouse under §5. A rejected pickup is escalated to a lead immediately rather than left as a failed attempt, since it usually means the ticket needs a second look, not just a retry.

input: Can you explain how the company policy handles cancellation and refunds for duplicate orders caused by payment timeouts versus genuine separate orders? For example, if a customer placed two orders for the X200 Cordless Vacuum using UPI, and one was a duplicate due to a timeout, what is the refund process and timeline?
expected_output: The policy states that if two confirmed orders result from a payment-gateway timeout and are clearly duplicates, the duplicate order is canceled before dispatch wherever possible. If both have already dispatched, the second order is treated as a company-caused return with a reverse pickup at no cost and a full refund including any shipping charged (Order Lifecycle Policy > 3). Genuine separate orders are handled normally without this special cancellation and refund process.
context:
POLICY order-lifecycle-policy.md (sales) — Order Lifecycle Policy

Order Lifecycle Policy

This policy governs the order itself: when it becomes binding, how it may change, and what happens when we cannot fulfil what we confirmed. It does not cover price or promotions (sales), payment mechanics (payments), or what happens after dispatch (shipping, delivery, returns, reverse).

Order Lifecycle Policy > 3. Duplicate Orders From a Retry

Where a checkout retry, a double-tap, or a payment-gateway timeout results in two confirmed orders for what was clearly meant to be one purchase, the customer is never made to receive and return both to get a refund. Cancel the duplicate before dispatch wherever possible; where both have already dispatched, the second is treated as a company-caused return under returns §4 — reverse pickup at no cost, full refund including any shipping charged on it. This is distinct from a genuine second order the customer separately intended to place, which is handled normally.

Order Lifecycle Policy > 6. Pre-Orders, Backorders and COD Availability

A pre-order or backorder commits to a delivery window given at the time of order; where that window will be missed, the customer is told before it passes (comms §5) and may cancel for a full and immediate refund at any point while still waiting, not only after the missed date. Cash on delivery is offered on orders up to **₹20,000**; above that value, a prepaid payment method is required, and this is disclosed at checkout rather than discovered as a rejected order. Where COD eligibility has been withdrawn from a specific account under fraud §3, that is a decision recorded there, not a general policy exception created here.

input: I have an issue with my order number 12345 for the X200 Cordless Vacuum. The package seems lost, and I want to know how claims are handled differently if passive package logging is available or not. I paid 5,000 Rupees via UPI. Could you please explain the remedy, the amount involved, and the timeline based on company policy?
expected_output: According to Shipping & Delivery Policy §2, if tracking shows "delivered" but you did not receive the package, a carrier claim is filed immediately. If passive package logging (e.g., security desk or smart-lockbox) is available and shows no record of delivery, this is treated as presumptive carrier loss, and you are eligible for a replacement or refund without waiting for the carrier's claim outcome. The policy does not specify a Rupee amount for claims but implies a full refund or replacement of the paid amount (5,000 Rupees). Turnaround times depend on carrier claim processing or expedited replacement eligibility under §4, which allows for express or same-day replacement at no extra charge if a time-sensitive reason is stated.
context:
POLICY shipping-delivery-policy.md (shipping) — Shipping & Delivery Policy

Shipping & Delivery Policy

This policy governs delivery timing, lost packages, transit damage, and expedited remedies — whether a shipment arrived, arrived late, or arrived damaged. Wrong item, missing item, partial delivery, a tampered parcel, or a failed delivery attempt are accuracy and access failures and are handled under delivery §1–§5 instead.

Shipping & Delivery Policy > 2. Lost Package Claims

If tracking shows "delivered" but the customer states the package was not received, a carrier claim should be filed immediately rather than waiting out an internal investigation window. In cases where the delivery address has passive package logging (a residential society's security desk, a building watchman's register, a mailroom, or a smart-lockbox with photo confirmation) and no corresponding log entry exists, this is treated as presumptive carrier loss — the customer should not be required to wait for the carrier's claim outcome before receiving a replacement or refund.

Shipping & Delivery Policy > 4. Expedited Replacement Eligibility

Customers who state a time-sensitive reason (upcoming move, event, medical need) for a damaged or lost shipment are eligible for expedited (express or same-day where available) replacement shipping at no additional charge, at agent discretion, without requiring proof of the stated reason.

input: Why did my refunded AV-450 credit expire as promotional credit, and how can it be restored? My order number is 123456, and I paid using UPI.
expected_output: Your refunded AV-450 credit should not expire as promotional credit because refund credits never expire, as stated in Wallet, Store Credit & Stored Value Policy > 2. Promotional Credit vs. Refunded Credit, and Their Expiries. If your refunded credit expired, it may have been mistakenly classified as promotional credit. Please contact support to have the balance reviewed and restored accordingly.
context:
POLICY stored-value-policy.md (billing) — Wallet, Store Credit & Stored Value Policy

Wallet, Store Credit & Stored Value Policy

This policy governs money and value we hold on a customer's behalf rather than money already in their bank account: wallet balance, store credit, gift cards, coupons and loyalty points. It answers what each is worth, when it expires, and when it may substitute for a cash refund.

Wallet, Store Credit & Stored Value Policy > 2. Promotional Credit vs. Refunded Credit, and Their Expiries

Credit issued as a **refund** (money the customer is owed back) never expires — it is their money, held in a different form, and an expiry on it would be the same as simply not refunding them after enough time passed. Credit issued as **promotional or goodwill value** (a bonus, a save-offer sweetener, a goodwill gesture the customer accepted as credit rather than cash) expires 12 months from issue, disclosed to the customer at the time it is given. The two must never be merged into one balance without distinguishing which portion is which, because a customer disputing an expired balance is entitled to know whether what expired was ever refundable money in the first place.

Wallet, Store Credit & Stored Value Policy > 4. Coupon Reissue When an Order Is Cancelled or Refunded

Where an order that used a coupon is cancelled or fully refunded, the coupon is reissued to the customer automatically if it was single-use and has not expired, so they are not penalised twice — once by losing the order, again by losing the discount. Any agent may manually trigger a reissue where the automatic process fails, without approval.

input: After paying ₹5,000 via UPI for the X200 Cordless Vacuum, what remedies are available and what is the escalation timeline?
expected_output: The provided context does not contain information regarding remedies or escalation timelines related to payments or the X200 Cordless Vacuum. According to AI-Assisted Drafting & Human Review Policy > 3, when the corpus does not answer, the assistant must not infer or generalize but refer the ticket under escalation §1. Therefore, no grounded answer can be provided based on the current policy.
context:
POLICY ai-drafting-policy.md (company-wide) — AI-Assisted Drafting & Human Review Policy

AI-Assisted Drafting & Human Review Policy

This policy is company-wide and governs the assistant that retrieves from the knowledge base and drafts replies. It exists because a fluent, confident, wrong answer is more dangerous than an obviously incomplete one, and because the person who presses send owns what it says.

AI-Assisted Drafting & Human Review Policy > 3. When the Corpus Does Not Answer

The correct behaviour when retrieval finds nothing adequate is to say so — to the agent, not to the customer — and stop. The assistant must not infer a threshold from a neighbouring one, average two cases into a rule, generalise from a single case to a policy, or reason from what a reasonable company would probably do. Where the corpus is silent, the ticket is referred under escalation §1, and the gap itself is recorded so the corpus can be fixed (kb §5). A visible "I don't have a basis for this" is the most valuable output this system produces, because it is the one an agent can act on safely.

AI-Assisted Drafting & Human Review Policy > 6. Review Is Recorded

Every draft records what the reviewer did with it — accepted, edited, or rejected — and an edit or rejection records why: the wrong case was retrieved, the wrong policy was cited, the tone was wrong, or something else. This is not administrative overhead; it is the only systematic signal about where retrieval and generation fail, and a review culture that accepts everything produces a system nobody can improve. Reviewers are measured on the quality of what they send, never on how fast they clear drafts.

input: Can you explain how the policy differentiates between advertised price errors and bulk/business pricing validity periods, especially in cases involving products like the X200 Cordless Vacuum or AV-450, and payments made via UPI or card?
expected_output: The policy states that the advertised price visible at order time is binding and must be honoured unless it is a clearly implausible system error (pricing §2). Bulk and business pricing quotes are valid for 30 days from issue and honoured within that period, without creating ongoing entitlements (pricing §5). Payment methods like UPI or card do not affect these rules.
context:
POLICY sales-pricing-policy.md (sales) — Pricing, MRP & Promotion Policy

Pricing, MRP & Promotion Policy

This policy governs what a customer is entitled to pay: the price itself, promotions and coupons, and price-match requests. What the order actually contains and its lifecycle after payment is orders §1–§8; what the product page promised beyond price is catalog §1–§5.

Pricing, MRP & Promotion Policy > 2. The Advertised Price Is Binding

If a price was live and visible to the customer at the time they ordered, that is the price they are entitled to, whether or not our systems applied it and whether or not it was the price we intended — provided it does not exceed MRP under §1. A misconfigured promotion, a pricing rule that failed on a bundle, a stale banner, a coupon that did not survive checkout — none of these are the customer's error and none of them transfer to the customer to fix. Honour the advertised price and adjust the order under billing §3. The one exception is a price so far below plausible that it is self-evidently a system fault rather than an offer (a decimal-point error, a currency mix-up); those are declined with an explanation and escalated to sales, never silently cancelled.

Pricing, MRP & Promotion Policy > 5. Quotes, Bulk and Business Pricing

A written quote for a bulk or business order is valid for **30 days** from issue unless it states otherwise, and is honoured within that period even if list pricing moves. Bulk and business pricing is quoted per order and does not create a standing entitlement to the same rate on the next one. Volume commitments, rebates and channel terms belong to the partner policy (partner §8), not to individual order handling.

input: As a support agent, how should I handle a complaint about the X200 Cordless Vacuum, order ID 12345, to ensure minimal data collection, no delay in response, and routing to the correct department according to company policy?
expected_output: According to complaint intake-policy.md §3, capture the subject, the customer's account, a contact method, and the order ID 12345 as it is product-related. Do not delay acknowledging the complaint even if any information is missing. Then, per §7, if automated classification predicts a department with confidence ≥0.60, route directly; otherwise, send for human review to avoid misrouting. This ensures minimal data collection, prompt response, and correct routing.
context:
POLICY complaint-intake-policy.md (company-wide) — Complaint Intake & Classification Policy

Complaint Intake & Classification Policy

This policy is company-wide and governs the first minute of every complaint: what we accept, what we must capture, and which department the ticket belongs to. Getting this wrong is expensive in a way that is hard to see later — a misrouted ticket is not just delayed, it is answered by people whose policy does not apply to it.

Complaint Intake & Classification Policy > 3. What We Capture, and What We Never Wait For

Every ticket needs a subject, the customer's account of what happened in their own words, and a way to reach them. Beyond that, capture what the remedy will need: the **order ID** for anything order- or product-related (this is the primary identifier — orders §1), the batch code for a quality or safety report (qa §2), the transaction reference for a payment dispute (payments §2). Ask for what is missing — but **never delay acknowledging a complaint because a field is empty.** Acknowledgement is not conditional on the customer having filled in our form correctly, and a first response that only asks for information the customer already gave us is worse than none. Collect the minimum the remedy requires and no more (privacy §1).

Complaint Intake & Classification Policy > 7. Automated Classification and the Confidence Floor

Where a department is predicted automatically, a confidence of **0.60 or above** is routed to that department directly. Below 0.60, the ticket goes to human review rather than to the most likely department — a wrong confident route costs more than a short queue, because the receiving department reads it against the wrong policy and answers accordingly. A near-tie between two departments above the floor goes to the higher-priority one under §5, not to the marginally higher score. Automated classification never sets severity: that is assessed under severity §3, and it never closes or resolves anything (§9).

input: Can you please provide the delivery ETA and current issue status for my X200 Cordless Vacuum? My order number is 123456, and I paid using UPI.
expected_output: Thank you for your inquiry. We acknowledge your request and are currently reviewing the status of your X200 Cordless Vacuum order. As per sla §6, we will provide you with an update on the delivery ETA and issue status within the agreed turnaround time. If there is any delay, we will inform you promptly with a revised date as outlined in sla §4.
context:
POLICY customer-communication-policy.md (company-wide) — Customer Communication & Tone Policy

Customer Communication & Tone Policy

This policy is company-wide and governs what we send to customers and how it reads. It applies to every outbound message regardless of who or what composed it, including assistant-drafted replies (ai §2).

Customer Communication & Tone Policy > 3. Internal Information Stays Internal

Departmental guidance is written for colleagues and is never forwarded verbatim. The following do not appear in customer-facing text under any circumstances:  
- **Incident and bug identifiers**, and internal ticket references of any kind.
- **Open investigations** — batch reviews, quality investigations, root-cause work in progress (qa §6).
- **Contract manufacturer, plant and component identifiers** (manufacturing §5).
- **Internal agent notes, guidance text and approval discussions.**
- **Any reference to another customer's report**, including counts of similar reports.
- **Employee names beyond the agent handling the ticket**, and never a name attached to a fault.  
The customer-facing version of "known integration gap, see INC-2291" is "a system fault on our side stopped your cancellation from reaching billing" — the same truth, without the internal record. Say what is true and useful about *their* case; say nothing about our internals.

Customer Communication & Tone Policy > 6. Silence Is the Worst Message

Acknowledge before resolving, and update on the cadence in sla §6 whether or not there is progress. Where a target will be missed, the customer hears it from us first, with a new date (sla §4). "We don't have an answer yet, here is when we will" is a complete and acceptable message; nothing at all is not.

input: As a support agent handling a complaint about order number 12345 for the X200 Cordless Vacuum paid via UPI, how does our data privacy policy restrict sharing order details and updates with the customer during complaint resolution?
expected_output: According to Data Privacy, PII & Records Retention Policy > 3. Need to Know, access to complaint details is limited to what the question requires, and unrelated order history or other tickets must not be accessed or shared. Additionally, per clause 6. Redaction Before the Knowledge Base, order and payment references like order number 12345 and payment method details must never be included in shared updates beyond what is necessary for resolution and must be redacted before the complaint enters the knowledge base.
context:
POLICY data-privacy-policy.md (company-wide) — Data Privacy, PII & Records Retention Policy

Data Privacy, PII & Records Retention Policy

This policy is company-wide and governs personal data in the complaint system: what we collect, what must never be written down, who may see it, how long we keep it, and what has to be removed before a resolved complaint becomes part of the knowledge base. It reflects our obligations as a data fiduciary under the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act 2023.

Data Privacy, PII & Records Retention Policy > 3. Need to Know

Access follows the ticket, not the customer: a department answering a referral sees the complaint and what the question needs, not the account's full order history, other tickets, or unrelated correspondence. Do not pull an account record to satisfy curiosity about a complaint, and do not quote one customer's history to another in the same household or business. Every access is attributable, and access to a ticket under legal hold is restricted to those Legal names.

Data Privacy, PII & Records Retention Policy > 6. Redaction Before the Knowledge Base

A resolved complaint enters the case corpus for its reasoning, never for its participants. Before it is admitted (kb §7), remove or replace:  
- **Names**, of the customer and of anyone they mention.
- **Contact details** — phone numbers, email addresses, delivery addresses.
- **Order, transaction, account and payment references**, and the last four digits of a card. These are directly re-identifying and are replaced with a placeholder, not shortened.
- **Serial numbers**, replaced with the batch or model prefix, which is what makes the case useful without identifying the unit's owner.
- **Free-text personal circumstances** — the health condition, the bereavement, the address arrangement. The fact that a courtesy exception was granted is retrievable and useful; the reason it was granted is not.  
What must survive redaction is the complaint's shape, the policy applied, and the outcome. A case that has to keep a customer's identity to make sense has not been redacted properly and does not belong in the corpus.

input: My X200 Cordless Vacuum order paid via UPI has not arrived yet. I've checked the status and payment trace. Please specify the remedy, timeline for delivery, and criteria for referral if applicable.
expected_output: The remedy for a missing order like your X200 Cordless Vacuum paid via UPI involves first confirming payment and shipment status as you have done. If the order is confirmed shipped but not delivered within the expected timeframe, a refund or replacement may be authorized. According to escalation-policy.md §3, any referral must include the specific question, customer statement, checks done (payment trace, order status), remedy considered, and what the customer has been told. If the issue requires a second referral, per §6, it must escalate to a lead to avoid repeated back-and-forth. Delivery timelines depend on shipment status but are not specified here.
context:
POLICY escalation-policy.md (company-wide) — Escalation & Department Referral Policy

Escalation & Department Referral Policy

This policy is company-wide and governs when a complaint is referred to another department. The company measures the share of complaints resolved without a referral, so the decision this policy makes is the one the business watches most closely — and the goal is fewer referrals through better knowledge, never fewer referrals through agents guessing.

Escalation & Department Referral Policy > 3. What a Referral Must Contain

A referral that cannot be answered without a conversation has not saved anyone time. It must state:  
- **The question**, specifically — not "please advise" but the decision being asked for.
- **What the customer said**, in their words, and what they have asked for.
- **What has already been checked** — the policy clauses consulted, the diagnostic steps recorded (tech_support §7), the records already pulled (order status, payment trace, tracking history).
- **The remedy under consideration** and why the agent cannot authorise it.
- **What the customer has been told so far**, including any date they have been given.

Escalation & Department Referral Policy > 6. One Referral, Then a Lead

A ticket may be referred back for clarification once. If a second round is needed, the ticket goes to a lead, because a question asked twice without a usable answer is a policy gap rather than a communication problem — and the customer has now been waiting through two turnarounds. Repeated referral between two departments on one ticket is prohibited: if ownership is genuinely disputed — an order that never arrived, where shipping, delivery and payments could each claim it is not theirs, is the most common example — a lead assigns it and the assignment is final for that ticket.

input: Can I get a goodwill replacement for my defective X200 Cordless Vacuum ordered with COD while my account is under review?
expected_output: While your account is under review, discretionary generosity such as goodwill replacements pauses, so a goodwill replacement for your X200 Cordless Vacuum ordered with COD will be declined (fraud-abuse-policy §3). However, any warranty defect is still remedied under warranty §2 without delay.
context:
POLICY fraud-abuse-policy.md (company-wide) — Fraud, Abuse & Repeat-Claim Policy

Fraud, Abuse & Repeat-Claim Policy

This policy is company-wide and governs the small number of accounts whose claim or order pattern is not explained by bad luck. It is written to protect margin without turning the queue into an interrogation, because the cost of treating honest customers as suspects is far larger than the losses it would prevent.

Fraud, Abuse & Repeat-Claim Policy > 3. What a Review Changes, and What It Cannot

While an account is under review, **discretionary generosity pauses**: goodwill is withheld (retention §4), courtesy exceptions outside the return window are declined, and the next claim of the flagged type requires evidence or lead approval before the remedy is issued. Where COD abuse is confirmed, COD may be withdrawn for that account under orders §6, leaving prepaid payment methods available.  
What does not change, at all: **anything the customer is entitled to.** A warranty defect is still remedied under warranty §2, a duplicate charge still refunded under billing §5, a statutory right still honoured under legal §8, and **every safety remedy is issued immediately regardless of any review, flag or pattern** (product_safety §4). We do not put a customer at risk to protect margin. Nor is a review a licence to slow a ticket down: the targets in sla §2 and §3 apply unchanged.

Fraud, Abuse & Repeat-Claim Policy > 6. Units We Did Not Sell

Where a serial number does not appear in our sales records — a grey-market unit, one from an unauthorised reseller, a counterfeit — warranty and returns do not apply, and service is available on a paid basis under spare_parts §4. Tell the customer plainly what we can and cannot do and why, without implying they did anything wrong; most people buying from an unfamiliar marketplace listing do not know who they bought from. **Safety obligations are not conditional on provenance**: a hazard report on a unit we did not sell still receives stop-use instructions, still gets its batch logged, and still reaches Product Safety under product_safety §1.

context:

COMPLAINT:
We're a retail partner and received a wholesale shipment of 50 units of the ProBlend 300 mixer (batch #MB-2291, order #WS-3390). input: Does the internal review for batch X200-2025Q1 of the X200 Cordless Vacuum authorize immediate refunds for issues like overheating and smoke incidents? If so, what is the refund amount and timeline, and does it apply to payments made via UPI, card, or COD?

context:

input: Can we authorize a no-return replacement for an X200 Cordless Vacuum that was damaged during transit, valued at ₹12,000 or more, as per shipping policy section 3.1?
expected_output: No, a no-return replacement for transit damage valued at ₹12,000 or more requires Admin or Lead approval, as Agents can only authorize replacements under ₹12,000 (shipping §3.1).
context:
POLICY agent-authority-policy.md (company-wide) — Agent Authority & Approval Matrix

Agent Authority & Approval Matrix

This policy is company-wide and answers one question: what may I do without asking? It **defines no limits of its own** — every value below is set by the policy that owns it, and this document is the single place to read them together. Where this matrix and an owning policy ever disagree, the owning policy is right and this one is out of date.

Agent Authority & Approval Matrix > 2. The Matrix

| Action | Agent | Lead | Admin | Limit defined in |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Refund of a documented charge | up to ₹8,000 | above ₹8,000 | above ₹8,000 | billing §1 |
| Goodwill credit or wallet credit | up to ₹4,000 | ₹4,001–₹15,000 | above ₹15,000 | retention §2 |
| Replacement without return — transit damage | under ₹12,000 value | at or above ₹12,000 | at or above ₹12,000 | shipping §3.1 |
| Replacement without return — safety symptom | any value | — | — | product_safety §4 |
| Repair-or-replace choice on a warranty defect | yes | — | — | warranty §2.3 |
| Warranty remedy without physical inspection | under ₹12,000 value | at or above ₹12,000 | at or above ₹12,000 | warranty §6 |
| On-site service visit authorisation | yes | — | — | warranty §7, §8 |
| RTO/failed-delivery redelivery waiver | yes | — | — | delivery §6 |
| Reverse-pickup self-ship reimbursement | up to ₹500 | above ₹500 | above ₹500 | reverse §3 |
| Oversell automatic inconvenience credit | yes (fixed amount) | — | — | orders §4 |
| Manual payment reversal outside standard reconciliation | no | no | yes | payments §6 |
| Coupon or wallet credit reissue after cancellation/refund | yes | — | — | stored_value §4 |
| Courtesy return outside the window | up to 10 days past, once per account | beyond 10 days | beyond 10 days | returns §1, §3 |
| Restocking consideration on an opened return | yes, at discretion | — | — | returns §2 |
| Free spare part under warranty | yes | — | — | spare_parts §2 |
| Honouring an advertised or coupon price | yes, subject to MRP | — | — | sales §1, §2, §3 |
| Post-purchase price adjustment | inside 14 days | outside 14 days | outside 14 days | sales §4 |
| Competitor price match | no | no | yes | sales §4 |
| Loyalty or save offer | within the published tiers | outside the tiers | outside the tiers | retention §5 |
| Severity upgrade | yes, immediately | — | — | severity §4 |
| Batch quarantine | no | no | manufacturing only | manufacturing §3 |
| Partner or marketplace-channel disruption credit | up to 5% of order | up to 5% | above 5% | partner §4 |
| Account restriction for abuse | no | no | yes | fraud §8 |
| Account unblock/order-block after a compromise report | yes, immediately | — | — | account §5 |
| Bulk remedy across an incident cohort | no | no | incident owner | incident §4 |  
Where a customer's situation qualifies under two rows, the more generous applies — a safety symptom overrides the transit-damage value threshold, as shipping §3.1 already states.

Agent Authority & Approval Matrix > 5. Splitting to Stay Under a Limit

Issuing two remedies where one was needed, splitting a refund across tickets, or pairing a small refund with a small credit to avoid a sign-off is a policy breach regardless of whether the total was reasonable and regardless of intent. The limits exist so that spend above a line is visible; a split hides it. Where the right remedy is above authority, ask — approval is fast, and a well-argued request above a limit is the system working correctly rather than a failure to cope.
